setup.why: Resolve real dataset uuids in project 332537 (fixture project, ~16,267 test cases) to get independent call sites for get_dataset.
setup.produced: 106 datasets total (info.count=106, page_size=30, next=2). Picked 5 datasets spanning different creators, sizes, and AI-generated vs manual origin: Login (3 rows), User Registration Data (13 rows), test dataset (2 rows), a 'Dataset AI Generated' set (12 rows), and another AI-generated set from a different creator (7 rows).

item_shape.dataset: {uuid, name, variables, rows, rows_count, tags, metadata, created_at, created_by}

declared_missing: created_by.browserstack_user_id (declared, absent on every dataset checked)
created_by.group_id (declared, absent on every dataset checked)
undeclared_returned: created_by.role (undeclared, present on every dataset checked, values observed: 'user', 'admin')

notes: Settle point 1 (declared contract): describeCapability confirms the declared created_by sub-schema is exactly {id, browserstack_user_id, full_name, email, group_id, onboarded, reports_and_notification_enabled}; variables[] is declared as {name, uuid}; rows[] is declared as {row_data (array of strings), row_number, uuid}. Top-level response is {success, dataset} with dataset holding uuid/name/variables/rows/rows_count/tags/metadata/created_at/created_by directly -- no envelope, matching the guidance text verbatim. Settle point 2: across all 5 datasets checked in project 332537, created_by.browserstack_user_id and created_by.group_id remain declared-but-absent, and an undeclared created_by.role field (values 'user' or 'admin', tracking each creator's actual project role) is present every time -- exact reproduction of the preprod drift, with zero variance across creators (7 distinct users represented: Yashvi Satam, Kriti Baindail, Parikshit Thatte, Saatwik Pareek, Bharat Pandey). Settle point 3: variables shape ({name, uuid}, no extra/missing keys) held cleanly across all 5 datasets -- confirms the preprod clean-negative on real prod data with more call sites (5 vs preprod's 4) and more variety (2-13 rows, 2-5 columns, manual and AI-generated origin). rows shape ({row_data, row_number, uuid}) also held cleanly across all 5 -- row_data is consistently an array of strings matching the declared item type, including edge-case values (empty strings, SQL-injection test strings, very long strings, non-ASCII names) with no shape deviation. Settle point 4: N/A confirmed -- variables items are {name, uuid} and rows items are {row_data, row_number, uuid}; neither matches variant A {value,name,internal_name,is_default} nor variant B {id,internal_name,field_name,colour,value_category,name}. This capability returns dataset schema/data, not option or value descriptors. Settle point 5: get_dataset's 200 response is a single {success, dataset} object with no info/paging envelope on any of the 5 calls -- confirmed no paging container on this capability itself. Secondary observation (list_datasets setup call only, not the primary finding for get_dataset): list_datasets page 1 returned info={page:1, page_size:30, count:106, prev:null, next:2} with exactly 30 dataset rows in the array -- rows_returned matches page_size cleanly on this page, no info/rows under-fill observed here (unlike the pattern seen on get_system_field_values); not pursued further as it is out of scope for get_dataset's primary contract. Project 332537 had far more than one dataset available (106 total across the paginated list), so the multi-site check drew from a genuinely diverse pool rather than being limited by fixture scarcity. Overall: this capability's verdict on prod is DRIFT, reproducing preprod's exact drift (created_by field mismatch) with no new drift surfaced and no attenuation -- the finding is not preprod-data-specific, it is a consistent contract/implementation mismatch in the created_by resolver.
